content.comment_body: Client is experiencing their [product_name] controller constantly power cycling. When it turns on, a symbol flashes several times, then the time and I/Q indicators are displayed. After a few seconds, the device loses power, and the screen turns off. It stays off briefly, then powers on again, repeating the cycle. The menu can be accessed by pressing specific keys, and the device remains powered in the menu, allowing changes to settings without issue; however, once exiting the menu, the cycling resumes. Since the device is stable in the menu, a power supply issue seems unlikely. The user suspects the device hardware is failing but is checking here for any known solutions before proceeding.
From your photo, it looks like you have a first-generation [product_name] controller, produced around 1996. Consider upgrading to a newer model.

That's quite a rare model. It appears the coupling capacitor might be defective, which would require an electrician to fix. As another user mentioned, upgrading to a new controller would be a better solution. Greetings, [user_name]
Can anyone recommend a suitable replacement model?
